card.name: Agbadza
card.era: Derived from war dance Atrikpui; recreational form c. 1920s
card.tagline: Ewe recreational dance evolved from the Atrikpui war dance
card.profile: Agbadza is among the oldest musical types of the Southern Ewe of Ghana, Togo, Benin and parts of southwestern Nigeria, derived from the older war dance Atrikpui (Wikipedia; African Music Safari). As a social and recreational form it is open to all, and is performed at the Hogbetsotso festival, funerals and weddings. Performance has five sections: Banyinyi, Vutsortsor (main dance), Adzo, Hatsatsa (song cycle) and a final Vutsortsor, driven by the Sogo lead drum, kidi, gankogui bell and axatse rattle (Wikipedia).
card.insight: Ethnomusicologist David Locke of Tufts University has published critical-edition transcriptions of Agbadza drumming, and Ewe master drummer Gideon Foli Alorwoyie featured it in 1960s folkloric groups (Wikipedia).
